papers.title_in_file: Biomedical imaging - Quantum Computing Inc (Resource library, Research and publications)
papers.version_note: The text is a web page: a publication list with abstracts and citation lines, not a paper. It carries no page breaks, so it is one page.
papers.what_it_is: A vendor web page listing publications and patents (mostly from the Huang group) on nonlinear-optical and single-photon imaging, each with its abstract.

assertions.value: The authors report a QPMS-based 3D imager that reconstructs the 3D profile of an obscured scene with 0.0006 detected signal photons per pulse, despite 34-fold spectral-temporally overlapping noise photons within a 6 ps detection window.
assertions.anchor: Noise-tolerant single photon sensitive three-dimensional imager, abstract, p.1
quotes: With only 0.0006 detected signal photons per pulse, we reliably reconstruct the 3D profile of an obscured scene, despite 34-fold spectral-temporally overlapping noise photons, within the 6 ps detection window
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study, given only as an abstract on a vendor page.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum parametric mode sorting (QPMS) can achieve signal to noise exceeding by far what is possible with typical linear optics filters.
assertions.anchor: Noise-tolerant single photon sensitive three-dimensional imager, abstract, p.1
quotes: quantum parametric mode sorting (QPMS) can achieve signal to noise exceeding by far what is possible with typical linear optics filters
assertions.certainty_reason: A description by the authors of their own technique; the abstract gives no comparison data.

assertions.value: The conference abstract reports noise-tolerant imaging with 8 dB noise rejection beyond the theoretical limit of linear-optical matched filters, from 0.0006 detected signal photons per pulse with 50-folds stronger background noise.
assertions.anchor: Noise-tolerant 3D Imaging, CLEO: Science and Innovations JTh5A.10, 2019
quotes: We demonstrate noise-tolerant 3D imaging with 8 dB noise rejection beyond the theoretical limit of linear-optical matched filters.
only 0.0006 detected signal photons per pulse despite being swamped by 50-folds stronger background noise
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one conference abstract.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstracts give 34-fold noise (Nature Communications) and 50-folds (CLEO) for the same 0.0006 photons per pulse; the page does not say whether the settings differ.

assertions.value: The authors report single photon sensitive non-invasive imaging of targets occluded by strongly scattering media with optical thicknesses reaching 9.5l_s (19l_s round trip), of a target 130 cm away, with millimeter lateral and depth resolution, requiring one photon detection out of 50,000 probe pulses.
assertions.anchor: Non-invasive single photon imaging through strongly scattering media, abstract, p.1
quotes: optical thicknesses reaching 9.5l_s (19l_s round trip)
diffraction-limited imaging of a target placed 130 cm away through the opaque media, with millimeter lateral and depth resolution while requiring only one photon detection out of 50,000 probe pulses
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study, abstract only.

assertions.value: The authors report a photon-sensitive camera using sum-frequency upconversion with an electron-multiplying CCD, with sub-millimeter depth resolution, reconstructing surface profiles of occluded targets behind obscurants of 14 optical depth (round trip) using only milliwatt illumination power.
assertions.anchor: Near-infrared 3D imaging with upconversion detection, abstract, p.1
quotes: it achieves sub-millimeter depth resolution, exceptional noise suppression, and high detection sensitivity
obscurants of 14 optical depth (round trip), using only milliwatt illumination power
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study, abstract only.

assertions.value: The authors report non-line-of-sight imaging and position retrieval of obscured objects around a corner, needing 4 x 10^-3 detected photons per pulse for each pixel, and resolving vibration frequencies of different objects from photon number fluctuation within a ten-picosecond window.
assertions.anchor: Single photon imaging and sensing of highly obscured objects around the corner, abstract, p.1
quotes: only 4 × 10^−3 photons are needed to be detected per pulse for each pixel
photon number fluctuation received within a ten-picosecond window, allowing NLOS acoustic sensing
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study, abstract only.

assertions.value: The authors report that a Laguerre-Gaussian signal mode can be converted with up to 60 times higher efficiency than an overlapping, but orthogonal, mode, by preparing the pump wave in an optimized spatial profile.
quotes: a mode can be converted with up to 60 times higher efficiency than an overlapping, but orthogonal, mode
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study, abstract only.

assertions.value: The authors report that with 40 projection modes the classification accuracy reaches 99.49% for the MNIST handwritten digit images, and up to 95.32% when the images are mixed with strong noise, using mode-selective image up-conversion, single-pixel detection and a deep neural network.
assertions.anchor: Single-pixel pattern recognition with coherent nonlinear optics, abstract, p.1
quotes: With 40 projection modes, the classification accuracy reaches a high value of 99.49%
up to 95.32%, even when they are mixed with strong noise
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study, abstract only; the dataset is a standard digit benchmark.
assertions.reader_inference: The ML step is a classical deep neural network applied to optically extracted features; the quantum content is not the classifier.

assertions.value: The authors report, verified by simulation on MNIST, that a partial Fourier transform raises accuracy from 81.25% (Fourier-domain processing) to 99.23%, and that the classifier reaches 83% accuracy for contaminated images whose signal-to-noise ratio is only -17dB.
assertions.anchor: Robust and efficient single-pixel image classification with nonlinear optics, abstract, p.1
quotes: it boosts accuracy from 81.25% (by Fourier-domain processing) to 99.23%
achieves 83% accuracy for highly contaminated images whose signal-to-noise ratio is only −17dB
assertions.certainty_reason: A simulation result from one study, abstract only.

assertions.value: The authors report that reconstructed handwritten-digit images reach a peak signal-to-noise ratio of approximately 20 dB and a structural similarity index measure of around 0.85, using mode-selective frequency upconversion, single-pixel detection and a deep neural network.
assertions.anchor: Single-pixel image reconstruction using coherent nonlinear optics, abstract, p.1
quotes: a peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) reaching approximately 20 dB and a structural similarity index measure (SSIM) of around 0.85
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study, abstract only.

assertions.value: The authors report that 32x32 pixel images of non-line-of-sight targets are reconstructed by a convolutional neural network from 8x8 scanning points, a downsampling ratio of 6.25%, with the network trained purely on simulated data.
assertions.anchor: Compressive Non-Line-of-Sight Imaging with Deep Learning, Physical Review Applied 19 (3), 034090, 2023
quotes: (32× 32 pixels) of the NLOS targets can be reconstructed
using significantly downscaled data (8× 8 scanning points) at a downsampling ratio of 6.25%
The CNN is end-to-end trained purely using simulated data
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study, abstract only.

assertions.value: The authors report selective upconversion of Laguerre-Gaussian spatial modes mixed with turbulent noise in lithium niobate, with extinction of about 40 dB without turbulence and about 20 dB in strong turbulence.
assertions.anchor: Mode selective up-conversion detection with turbulence, abstract, p.1
quotes: The extinction reaches ~40 dB without turbulence, and maintains ~20 dB in the presence of strong turbulence.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study, abstract only.

assertions.value: The authors report that optimizing pump temporal profiles achieves more than 12-dB extinction for mutually unbiased basis sets in a programmable spatiotemporal parametric mode sorter, and that coupling the up-converted light into a single-mode fiber or operating at the edge of phase matching improves mode-sorting performance.
assertions.anchor: Programmable Spatiotemporal Quantum Parametric Mode Sorter, abstract, p.1
quotes: improvement in the quantum mode-sorting performance by coupling the up-converted light into a single-mode fiber and/or operating the up-conversion at the edge of phase matching
Optimizing pump temporal profiles allows us to achieve more than 12-dB extinction
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study, abstract only.

assertions.value: The authors propose a chi-2 microdisk quantum switch; as an example, a 2.5-um-thick, 10 um radius GaAs microdisk with intrinsic Q of about 10^8 and fiber-cavity-coupling Q of about 10^4 could achieve low-loss (at most 1%) switching of gigahertz-rate O-band quantum signals with milliwatt-peak-power C-band pumps.
assertions.anchor: Interaction-free all-optical switching in χ(2)microdisks for quantum applications, abstract, p.1
quotes: a 2.5-μm-thick, 10μm radius GaAs microdisk with an intrinsic Q of ∼10^8 and a fiber-cavity-coupling Q of ∼10^4
low-loss (≲1%) switching for gigahertz-rate O-band quantum signals with milliwatt-peak-power pumps in the C band
assertions.certainty_reason: A design proposal stated in an abstract; the page shows no experiment.

assertions.value: The page is a publication and patent list: each entry gives an abstract or a short description, a link and a citation line, and the page gives no methods, data tables or full results for any entry.
quotes: Devices and methods for giant single-photon nonlinearities
Biomedical imaging Noise-tolerant single photon sensitive three-dimensional imager

assertions.reader_inference: Any figure taken from this page is an abstract-level claim and needs the linked paper before it is graded above low.
